w: At 6.10 p.m. Swamishri left Bochasan for Borsad, where a new assembly hall had been built. The murtis of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and the Guru Parampara for the assembly hall were positioned on the stage. Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha of the murtis.
A few youths from America, travelling with Swamishri, asked Swamishri a few questions.

Hari (N.J.) : You have been blessed by two great people (satpurush) – Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Which Satpurush are we blessed with? Swamishri : The same. How can there be any other? Whether you say Shastriji Maharaj or Yogiji Maharaj, are they different? Shriji Maharaj resides in them. They are Gunatit. They look different but their atma (chaitanya) is one. The same qualities of Maharaj are in Gunatitanand Swami, Bhagatji Maharaj, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Though they look different, in essence, they are Maharaj. Since they have the qualities of God they are the forms of God.

Jayesh (Jersey) : We have not seen Shriji Maharaj. We have not seen the form of Maharaj, so when we meditate on whom should we meditate? Swamishri: Everyone is included by meditating on and remembering Yogiji Maharaj. Whichever form one attains and loves, in that form God resides fully. So by meditating and remembering him, Maharaj is not being relegated. God is one, and He resides in and works through all. By having affection for Yogiji Maharaj, is the same as having affection for Maharaj. So he enjoins us in that form (Maharaj).

Vrajesh (Chicago) : Sometimes there is a feeling of void in doing devotion and service. How can we remain enthusiastic and fresh in faith? Swamishri : Are you not enthusiastic about worldly things? After seeing a worldly thing once, you still see it ten more times. The joy in seeing it each time is the same. The same men play cricket. Is there anything new in it? But you find it new and exciting all the time. Even in food, though it is the same you find it interesting. You always experience joy in it. Similarly, you should have same feelings for God’s discourses. When you are inclined towards food you find it tasty! Likewise, you should find God to be joyful and new.

Mahant Swami Maharaj was going from the entrance of the Swaminarayan Haveli towards the lift. Pointing to a large picture (photo) of Yogiji Maharaj, bare bodied, in the corridor, he said to Atmaswarupdas Swami, "Yogibapa had this photo taken sitting on the platform near the water tank at Akshar Bhuvan in Mumbai."

Hearing this, Atmaswarupdas Swami jumped with delight and said, "Swami! Today, as soon as I entered the Haveli, the question came to my mind, where must this photo have been taken? And knowing my inner thoughts, you instantly caught my thought and told me this."
"Once I recognised the one who knows all hearts, I was filled with longing..." Once we recognise the one who knows all hearts, how can we not be filled with longing for him?

Today in the evening assembly, first the Tarakwa High School was inaugurated by Mahant Swami Maharaj. After that, Masari Road, a main road of the Parklands area, was declared renamed "Pramukh Swami Avenue".
At the end of the assembly, crowning it, Swamishri began his blessings in English:

"Pramukh Swami Maharaj, about whom it was just said, 'In the joy of others lies our own, in the good of others lies our own, in the progress of others lies our own.' He actually lived every second of his life according to this. He did not just quote this once in a while, but he always followed the quote. He lived according to this (quote) every second of his life, night and day; that is an extraordinary thing. He actually lived his (whole) life (accordingly).

"He met everyone, whether poor or rich, with the same attitude. We differentiate, we see he's poor, he's rich, but Pramukh Swami Maharaj did not have that (attitude), he regarded everyone as equal, there was no discrimination in his mind. He (had) no differentiation in his mind. All are equal. He looked upon everyone as a human being; he did not differentiate (against anyone), so we (too) must do the same and live in the same way. Then unity, friendliness and oneness will come."

That is, "It has been said of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, 'In the joy of others lies our joy, in the good of others lies our good, in the progress of others lies our progress.' He lived every moment in this way. He did not merely speak this saying but followed it, lived it every moment, lived it day and night. This is an extraordinary thing.

"He met everyone, poor and rich, with the same feeling. We look at people as, this one is poor and this one is rich. But in Pramukh Swami Maharaj's mind there was no discrimination. He saw all equally. He saw everyone as a human being. We (too) must do the same and live in the same way. Then unity, friendliness and oneness will come."
This was the first historic occasion in the whole Gunatit tradition that the one seated as guru had given his blessings in English.
